description: Ambrosia is a Linux distro on Arch that looks and moves as one thing: one design authority, one token file, a generator theming every toolkit identically. It ships as Arch packages and an archiso installer image. The design system, preview and review site exist; the distro pipeline (packages, Ambrosia session on KWin, live image, installer) has a first cut; the shell has its menu bar and traffic-light window frames.
features: Single OKLCH token file drives every toolkit theme identically
Generates GTK, KDE, Aurorae, QML, fontconfig, web CSS, JSON from tokens
Gamut-maps colors to sRGB with contrast-derived accent variants
Solves response/damping springs into constants and easing curves
Validates contrast, concentric radii, and spacing grid via tests
Browser mock desktop preview and review site render spec with live specimens
Dark mode and accents via keys/URL; verdict threads in review
Installs themes per-user on Linux preserving prior configs
Mac-first keyboard: Super-as-Command, ⌘ glyphs in menus, Files shortcuts
Signed Arch pacman repo on GitHub; archiso installer, UEFI, QEMU-testable
Menu bar: focused-app menus with shortcuts, Wi-Fi, search, clock
Super+Space Spotlight; dock keeps pinned order, separate launchers, Mac-style Trash
Control center: pure blur glass, modes, sliding notification banners
Honey-bowl Ambrosia branding in menu bar, banner, favicon, preview and review site
Finder-style file manager: list, folders, menus, undo/redo copy/move/trash/rename, drag-drop
Starter apps: Firefox, Kate, Gwenview, Okular, Ark, Discover

preview.summary: Preview Desktop is a static HTML/JS mock macOS-like desktop for visually reviewing generated tokens. It renders draggable/focusable windows, menubar popups, sliders, control center, dock, and a live clock with no build step beyond `make build`. Every color, type, radius, shadow, and motion value comes from dist/web/tokens.css; preview.css holds only mock-desktop layout positions, and the menubar/README/favicon use the Ambrosia bowl logo while assets/ also holds the hand-drawn Files app icon.

Control center (capsule modules, toggles, sliders, Edit Controls)
Dock (padding, glassy icons, tooltip, badges, separators)
Theme and accent switching (D / A keys, URL params)
Files app icon (Finder-style two-tone face, Dock Files pin)

Toggle with D (dark mode) and A (accent cycle) to review

preview/preview.js — theme/accent switching, popups, draggable windows, sliders, clock, squircle mask
preview/preview.css — mock-desktop layout; all design values via var(--amb-*) / var(--glass-*)
preview/glass.css — shared glass recipe (tint, blur, rim, edge, specular ring, grain)
assets/ambrosia.svg — bowl-with-scoops-and-spoon brand mark used in menubar and preview
assets/icon.svg — app/favicon form of the bowl mark
assets/icons/org.ambrosia.files.svg — hand-drawn Files app icon on a blue squircle, matched to the macOS Dock grid
rules: Never hardcode design values in preview/*.css — use vars from dist/web/tokens.css; only layout positions may be literals.
Run `make build` first — preview is broken/stale without generated dist/web/tokens.css.
Do not add build tooling or JS dependencies — static HTML/JS only.
Keep glass.css shared-safe — it is also used by the review site, so no preview-specific layout in it.
Round inner panels (e.g. sidebar) to their own outer corners — scaled-down blur is cut to the window shape only if the panel itself is rounded, otherwise corners render sharp/square.
Keep file selection highlight behind the icon — replacing the document page fill with selection color turns clicked icons black.
Draw app icons by hand as our own vectors; never trace Apple's artwork, and keep reference screenshots of macOS only in the gitignored out/ folder.
edges: Design Tokens via dist/web/tokens.css — sole source of colors, type, radii, shadows, springs; preview breaks without a build
Build and Install — `make build` generates dist/web/tokens.css that preview links
Shell Dock and Packaging — the Files icon in assets/icons/org.ambrosia.files.svg is the Dock's Files pin and is installed by the package build

design-tokens.summary: Single-file source of truth for ambrosia's look and motion, exporting type scale, 4px spacing, radii, OKLCH colors, glass/materials, shadows, and springs. All dist themes are generated from it via tools/gen, so this file is edited instead of generated output. Newcomer must grasp: colors are OKLCH strings for perceptually even lightness and everything is light/dark Mode pairs.
files: design/tokens.ts — the single source of truth: font/type/tracking, space, radius, OKLCH color pairs, glass, shadow, springs
design/DESIGN.md — reasoning behind the numbers before retuning values
rules: Never hand-edit generated output in dist/; change design/tokens.ts and regenerate.
Keep colors as OKLCH strings (oklch(L C H) or with / A) so generator can convert and gamut-map to sRGB.
Provide both light and dark values via Mode/Pair for mode-dependent tokens.
See DESIGN.md for reasoning behind the numbers before retuning values.
Menus snap open instantly with no open animation (close fades 120ms); control-center panel is blur-only with no fill, border, or shadow, controls carry their own glass.
edges: Generator Core — resolves design/tokens.ts: OKLCH to sRGB, contrast, springs, dist orchestration
Theme Targets — format the resolved model into GTK, KDE, QML, fontconfig, web output
Preview Desktop — styled only from generated dist/web/tokens.css, never this file directly

review-site.summary: The Review Site is a design-review web app that renders every `## ` section of DESIGN.md/DECISIONS.md as a reviewable item with live specimens, a verdict and a notes thread. Specimens are built with the same tokens and resolver the generator ships, so review matches output. State lives in `design/review.json` via a Bun server when present, otherwise in browser localStorage; `build.ts` emits a static fallback into `dist/site/`.

map.name: Review items sourced from design docs
Site styling in own design language

main.ts renders section with reasoning plus specimens
review.ts load() tries /api/review, falls back to localStorage
user sets verdict / posts note via setVerdict/addMessage
server.ts queues write into design/review.json or local mode saves locally
onChange listeners re-render verdict and thread

steps: server.ts serves index.html with HMR on port 4747
STATIC preview/, dist/web/, assets/ served as plain files
client fetches /api/review for shared state
POST verdict/message serialized through one write queue

build-install.summary: This layer builds, tests and installs Ambrosia. Bun and TypeScript handle the build, Make orchestrates the targets, and a POSIX sh script installs the already-generated themes for the current Linux user into XDG config and data directories. Install copies from dist/ and backs up foreign files. The key idea: install never loses user data, since foreign files become <name>.before-ambrosia and ambrosia-owned files are overwritten silently. Make publish also pushes the signed Arch package repo to GitHub Releases.

map.name: Publish signed Arch package repo (make publish)
Running the build gate, review site and screenshots on tenet (make remote-build, review-remote, shot-remote)

flows.name: Install themes
steps: Resolve dist/ relative to script location
Exit early (success) on non-Linux, pointing at dist/
Detect GTK mode via gsettings color-scheme (default light)
place() each dist artifact into XDG_CONFIG_HOME / XDG_DATA_HOME, backing up foreign files

theme-targets.summary: This layer turns the resolved theme model (Resolved/ResolvedMode from Generator Core) into per-toolkit output files. Each file in tools/gen/targets/ is a pure formatter: roles/colors plus shared helpers. Newcomers must grasp that nothing is resolved here — token truth and color math live upstream; targets only map and serialize.

map.name: Session kdeglobals (light scheme + type-scale fonts as QFont strings)
KWin window decoration (Aurorae SVG theme: traffic lights, titlebar, window shadow)

flows.name: Resolved model to toolkit file
steps: Generator Core produces Resolved / ResolvedMode
Target maps roles to toolkit vocabulary (libadwaita vars, KDE sets, QML tree, CSS vars)
Colors serialized via color helpers (toCss, toKde, toQtHex) and shared helpers (HEADER, pt, fontStack, kebab/slug)
Formatter returns file string for dist orchestration to write

files: tools/gen/targets/shared.ts — shared header, kebab/slug, fontStack, cssShadow, pt helpers
tools/gen/targets/gtk.ts — libadwaita CSS vars (gtk4) and named colors per mode (gtk3)
tools/gen/targets/kde.ts — opaque .colors sets, translucency flattened onto background
tools/gen/targets/qml.ts — Ambrosia QML singleton tree with Theme.dark / Theme.accentName switching
tools/gen/targets/web.ts — --amb-* CSS custom properties for preview/web surfaces
tools/gen/targets/fontconfig.ts — sans-serif/monospace aliases and rasterization defaults
tools/gen/targets/aurorae.ts — Aurorae theme per mode: rc layout, nine-slice decoration.svg painted as PNGs (window color, rim, edge, box-shadows), vector button SVGs
rules: Do not edit generated output; every file carries HEADER pointing back to design/tokens.ts via tools/gen.
Do not resolve or derive colors here — use the passed Resolved model and color.ts / resolve.ts helpers.
KDE output must stay opaque r,g,b: flatten translucent values with flat() onto their background set.
GTK3 has no prefers-color-scheme: emit one file per mode; GTK4 emits light and dark in one file.
Keep QML identifiers safe: slug token keys and prefix leading digits.
QML property names can't be ECMAScript keywords; qml.ts suffixes them with _ (Theme.size.switch_), guarded by a test in tools/gen/rules.test.ts.

Aurorae makes KWin's window shadow from what decoration.svg paints in its Padding*, slicing it at the pieces' own sizes; KSvg only takes a prefix whose -center element exists, so each button state has both 'x' and 'x-center'. The frame is 1x PNG (soft on HiDPI).
edges: Design Tokens — reads type, color, font, shadow token definitions as input vocabulary
Generator Core — consumes Resolved/ResolvedMode and color/spring serializers (toCss, toKde, toQtHex, toCssLinear, flat)
Build and Install — dist orchestration writes formatter output to dist/ for install

shell-and-session.summary: The desktop shell (Quickshell QML on the generated Ambrosia Theme module) and the session that hosts it. startambrosia runs Plasma's session with XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP=ambrosia; systemd units keyed on that variable swap plasmashell for Quickshell, and /etc/xdg/ambrosia carries session-only KDE/KWin defaults. The shell is now functional, not just visual: menu bar with real app menus, Spotlight launcher on Super+Space, dock, control center and notification banners, and it must match preview/ visually.

shell/MenuBar.qml — menu bar container and menu switching
shell/Apps.qml — running-app / menu model for app menus and dock

shell/Popups.qml — what's open and where: menu levels, control center, confirmation, Search
rules: Build file URLs from Quickshell.shellDir with an explicit file:// — Quickshell's QML base URL is qrc:/qs-blackhole, so relative URLs and Qt.resolvedUrl don't reach files.
All values come from import Ambrosia (Theme.*); never hard-code colors or sizes that a token has.
Dock and Trash artwork is hand-drawn vector art; never copy or extract Apple's images from Dock.app or any system bundle.
Dock icons, including the Files icon, are our own drawings: never trace Finder.app or any macOS file; the face and shapes must be ours even when the squircle and colours match macOS.
The Dock's Trash is sized against its neighbouring icons by macOS's squircle-to-bin ratio; resize it with them, not on its own.

KWin gives its window list (org_kde_plasma_window_management) only to programs a desktop file grants, matched by Exec path: org.ambrosia.shell.desktop names /usr/bin/quickshell. No other desktop file may Exec /usr/bin/quickshell (KWin takes the first match), so shortcuts run /usr/bin/ambrosia.

Plasma's appmenu kded only collects apps' menus while org.kde.kappmenuview is on the bus; Apps.qml holds it with dbus-test-tool black-hole. Apps check at startup, so ones started before the shell keep their in-window menus.
A QML file loaded by file:// URL (Loader) gets its own copies of the shell's singletons; pass it values instead (AppMenu.qml).

Menus, the control center and confirmations draw on Overlay.qml, a grabbing PopupWindow of the menu bar: KWin sends it keys without activating it, so the app stays active (Search, a keyboard-taking layer surface, deactivates it). It spans the screen, bar strip masked: Qt hands an open popup the bar's pointer events by position. Apps.frozen holds the bar's app; window actions capture their window at open.
Compare a window with the screen it was made for (home), not its live screen, which changes as it maps and unmaps and loops through visible.
Start apps through kstart (Session.launch/run), never execDetached on the app: it would live in ambrosia-shell.service's cgroup and die when the shell restarts.
Pinned apps' AppId ends in .desktop, running ones' not (use Apps.entryFor). Windows keep their pin's Dock spot only with launchInPlace and separateLaunchers: true.

Glass.qml draws preview/glass.css: top-lit rim (ring: true for the Dock's all-round rim), a 135° specular ring, 0.5px edge, shadow outside only. Use it for any glass surface instead of a plain tinted Rectangle.

KWin's blur is global: [Effect-blur] BlurStrength and Saturation (integer, 100 = none) in session/xdg/kwinrc apply to every glass surface; the control center's untinted backdrop sets them (6, 100). Reload with /Effects reconfigureEffect blur, not KWin.reconfigure.

kdedefaults is rewritten only when the look-and-feel's name changes: Breeze settings go in session/xdg/breezerc; startambrosia copies the look-and-feel's decoration into kdedefaults/kwinrc each login.

packaging-and-image.summary: Everything that turns the repo into an installable, updatable distro. packaging/PKGBUILD builds ambrosia-keyring, ambrosia-theme, ambrosia-shell and ambrosia-desktop from the checkout; packaging/quickshell rebuilds Quickshell v0.3.2 with a patch so the menu bar can read apps' real menus, including each item's shortcut, and so apps learn when each menu opens. tools/publish-repo.sh (make publish, on the Mac) builds them on tenet, signs them with a key kept on the Mac, and uploads them to the hosted [ambrosia] pacman repo: the rolling repo release of the public github.com/justin06lee/ambrosia-packages. iso/ is an archiso profile (from Arch's releng) whose live system logs into Ambrosia and carries the packages as a local repo for its installer, which puts [ambrosia] first in the installed system's pacman.conf. Built on an Arch host (tenet), tested in a headless QEMU VM.

packaging/quickshell/dbusmenu-source.patch — DBusMenu source patch: item shortcuts, and AboutToShow on every menu open
rules: [ambrosia] must stay first in pacman.conf (the image's, and the installed one the installer writes): pacman takes a package from the first repo that has it, whatever the version, so our Quickshell only wins from there. ambrosia-shell needs quickshell-dbusmenu-source, which only our build provides.
Quickshell links Qt internals: when Arch updates qt6-base, bump pkgrel in packaging/quickshell/PKGBUILD and make publish (it rebuilds Quickshell when the release lacks that version).
Any change to dbusmenu-source.patch must update its checksum and bump pkgrel in packaging/quickshell/PKGBUILD, because make publish only rebuilds Quickshell for a version the release lacks.

The patch must make Quickshell send DBusMenu AboutToShow on every menu open, not only the first: Qt raises a menu's aboutToShow only from that call, so apps tracking open menus miss every later open otherwise.
packaging/PKGBUILD must install ambrosia-shell's pacman restart hook (session/ambrosia-shell-restart.hook); without it, upgraded shell QML waits for the next login to take effect.
App icons in assets/icons/ reach installed systems only if packaging/PKGBUILD installs them; a hand copy on tenet is replaced by the next package install, so a hand copy alone is not a fix.
Build and work dirs go under ~/work/ambrosia/out on /home (tenet's / has ~25 GB); makepkg's Quickshell source is out/build/quickshell/src/quickshell. mkarchiso needs root, makepkg refuses it.
The installer is UEFI-only and needs the internet (pacstrap pulls everything but our packages from Arch mirrors).
Ship pipewire-jack, not jack2: the two conflict and broke restore/install when both were pulled in.
tools/vm.sh must not forward host port 2222: makima uses it to reach tenet, so the test VM SSH forward lives on 10022.
The installer copies live Wi-Fi profiles without interface-name: the live image names the card wlan0 (iwd), the installed system by its predictable name (wlo1).

GitHub renames release assets with ':' or '~' (to '.'), so no epochs in our package versions; publish-repo.sh refuses such names. Assets can't be symlinks: ambrosia.db and .files are uploaded as real files.
Hand copies on tenet (shell/, /etc/xdg/ambrosia) go only through pacman -U --overwrite, never -Syu; after an install pacman -Qkk must show 0 altered files and no .pacnew.
edges: Shell and Session — ambrosia-shell ships shell/ and session/, including the pacman restart hook that session/ shell upgrades trigger; the Dock's Files icon (assets/icons/org.ambrosia.files.svg) is installed by the PKGBUILD; the menu bar's shortcut column reads item shortcuts from our patched Quickshell

generator-core.summary: Generator Core resolves design/tokens.ts into a concrete sRGB + solved-spring model that every target formats. It is built as Bun+TypeScript: color math, spring solver, a per-mode resolver, and a dist orchestrator. A newcomer must grasp that targets never read tokens directly; resolve() is the single agreement point for derived colors and motion.

map.name: OKLCH to sRGB conversion with gamut mapping
Window frame target registration (Aurorae traffic lights)

flows.name: Generate dist from tokens
steps: tools/gen/index.ts calls resolve()
resolve.ts parses OKLCH via color.ts and solves springs via spring.ts
index.ts passes Resolved model to each formatter in tools/gen/targets/ (including aurorae.ts)
Formatted strings written to dist/ paths (web, gtk, kde, qml, fontconfig, aurorae) plus resolved dump

flows.name: Derive a concrete color
steps: parseOklch() parses oklch() string
toLinear + gamut-mapped conversion to RGBA in color.ts
over()/withAlpha() composite translucency
contrast()/ensureContrast() enforce readability for accents and labels

files: tools/gen/resolve.ts — resolves tokens.ts into per-mode Resolved colors, accents, material, glass, shadows and springs
tools/gen/index.ts — orchestrates generation: resolves once, formats every target, writes dist/
tools/gen/color.ts — OKLCH parsing, OKLCH to sRGB with gamut mapping, compositing, contrast, and output formatters
tools/gen/spring.ts — solves (response, damping) springs into stiffness/damping, settle duration, and sampled curve
rules: Never read design/tokens.ts directly from a target for colors — go through resolve() so derived accents and flattened labels agree everywhere.
Never bypass color.ts gamut mapping and contrast helpers with ad-hoc conversion — out-of-gamut OKLCH and unreadable text result.
Keep Resolved/ResolvedMode/ResolvedAccent shapes stable — every formatter in tools/gen/targets/ depends on them.
edges: Design Tokens — sole input: reads design/tokens.ts types and values, never the reverse
Theme Targets — sole consumer: every formatter takes the Resolved model from resolve(); aurorae.ts builds the window frame from the same model
Build and Install — runs the generator to produce dist/ before install and test

files-app.summary: Files, Ambrosia's Finder: a frameless Qt Quick window drawn like macOS 26's Finder (floating sidebar, glass toolbar capsules, list and icon views, path bar, menus exported to the menu bar) over a C++20 core: getdents64 + parallel statx + natural-sort keys on worker threads for local folders, KIO for other URLs. Finder's measurements live in files/qml/Finder.qml; art is ours. Built, benchmarked and photographed on tenet with files/tools/tenet.sh (the Mac runs only editing and git); app id and icon name org.ambrosia.files are one contract with Shell and Session.

rules: The desktop id must be org.ambrosia.files, because Shell and Session pin the app by that name.
The desktop file's Icon= and the window icon must use the same name, org.ambrosia.files.
Import QtQuick.Controls.Basic only as a namespace (as Controls): its Label otherwise shadows files/qml/Label.qml.

Grab only on the headless KWin with Mesa software GL (files/tools/tenet.sh grab): Qt's offscreen platform falls back to the software scene graph, which drops MultiEffect shadows; tenet's GPU stays untouched.

Every build and benchmark on tenet runs capped (systemd-run MemoryMax=6G and -j2 for builds, 4G for probes; nice 19, ionice -c3) and stops when tenet is strained: it has no swap and hosts mira's gateway, and an uncapped ninja at 18 jobs once took it down. Watch it from the Mac with awk, not zsh word splitting.
tenet's /tmp is RAM-backed: keep Files scratch (fixtures, recorder, stills, grab helper) under /var/tmp or /root, never /tmp.
tenet.sh builds the Mac working tree's files/, uncommitted changes included, so it must not be pointed at a checkout that follows pushed commits.
Stop a running Files before copying a new build to tenet; otherwise the test runs the old binary.
Qt logs go to the journal when stderr isn't a terminal: set QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 to see QML errors over SSH.

Command is Ctrl in Files (what the Mac-first keyd remap hands apps); the window also accepts Super directly; DBusMenu exports Control, which the shell draws as ⌘ (r120). KWin grabs Meta+Up and Meta+Alt+L on tenet.
Menu actions must act on the window captured when the menu opened; the shell freezes the menu bar's app while a menu is open, so resolving the target at click time sends actions to the wrong window.
